sections.title: Proposed project
sections.value: The bounded review would be a QA Control Review of the affected QA cell.

sections.title: Business need
sections.value: Establish who owns command authorization, how retired tests remain controlled, and how evidence will be preserved for later decisions since these are traceable facts that the QA can review later and while a completed review is made it is not a promise of restored production

sections.title: Expected value and beneficiaries
sections.value: This will benefit the QA and engineers as the QA gets a clear record of the affected QA cell and preserve the evidence. Also the sponsor receives a Business case recommendation

sections.title: Included work
sections.value: The work I recommend is a review of the affected QA cell and the deliverables would be a one command ownership record, a scheduling and retirement control inventory and evidence preservation checklist

sections.title: Excluded work
sections.value: This review doesn't authorize the restarting or operating of MR-17, changing the software or test schedules and changing original records. Also it doesnt not authorize buying a replacement robot or choosing a vendor

sections.title: Technical feasibility
sections.value: The review can use the existing tools and read only record exports. The access has been requested but not confirmed yet

sections.title: Operational feasibility
sections.value: The work she be planned around the normal duties of the staff involved such as QA, engineers and the relevant record custodians who would need to make time to provide records. The sponsor should confirm the availability

sections.title: Cost and resource feasibility
sections.value: The base is $180 below the $3000 envelope. The estimated range is $2,350–$3,525, so the low end is within the envelope, but the high end is $525 over the limit. Excluded is equipment purchase, software licenses or overtime

sections.title: Schedule feasibility
sections.value: The plan depends on getting the needed read-only exports by day 3 so the review can continue as planned. Also the staff time adds up to 48 hours but it does not mean the review will take 48 hours of elapsed time as the staff can work different parts of the eight day schedule

sections.title: Known constraints
sections.value: The known budget is up to $3000 in internal staff time and proposed review schedule of 8 business days. Access still needs to be confirmed. For safety, all learner work must stay outside the safety glass, original records must be preserved, and only read-only copies should be used. Possible future events can include being denied

sections.title: Risks and assumptions
sections.value: One assumption that needs to be checked is whether the team will get access to the needed read-only exports by day 3. If the exports are late or access is denied, the review could take longer than the planned eight business days or need to be revised or deferred. The responsible person would be the one providing access to the exports

sections.title: Success measures and evidence
sections.value: The sponsor can check if the review was completed by looking if everything  requested was documented. The measures six request baseline differs from a proposed target as a proposed target is set for the future and is not a guaranteed result

sections.title: Rationale and conditions
sections.value: I would recommend advise because the higher estimate of 3,252 goes over the budget by 525 and also access to the read only exports have not been confirmed yet and it can affect the overall schedule. The tradeoff would be that revising could delay the review but it was it more cost effective and not going over the budget

sections.title: Next authorization or information step
sections.value: The sponsor should make the final decision and authorize any work. The sponsor can then decide whether to proceed, revise further, defer, or decline.
